entries.reason: the class is a strong-imported LOAD-FAIL for provenance and telegram; iOS 6.1.3 has no CSSearchableIndex-shaped system index, so this port keeps the journal itself, in a real per-index store under Application Support, and bridges it to the release's own Spotlight.framework private class SPSpotlightManager, whose pull model (startRecordUpdatesForApplication:andCategory:, requestRecordUpdatesForApplication:category:andIDs:, notifyIndexer) already serves Messages and Calendar on this release
entries.effect: isIndexingAvailable answers YES; defaultSearchableIndex and initWithName: give a real instance backed by its own plist store; indexSearchableItems:, the two delete methods and deleteAllSearchableItemsWithCompletionHandler: write or remove entries in that store and call their handler with a nil error; beginIndexBatch does nothing since the store commits synchronously, endIndexBatchWithClientState:completionHandler: persists the client state (refusing on the unbatched defaultSearchableIndex, per the header) and fetchLastClientStateWithCompletionHandler: reads it back; every mutation also registers the index's category with SPSpotlightManager and pushes the changed identifiers to it, best-effort and never fatal if the private class or its selectors are absent
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the contract; Spotlight.framework and Search.framework of the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3, disassembled with modules/apple/dyld.lua's extract
